sections.heading: 16.0 Introduction
sections.title: 16.0 Introduction
sections.text: Some support in living organisms is necessary to uphold and sustain the body against gravity and other external forces. As the living organisms increased in size through the process of evolution, the need for support became greater. This was particularly true once living organisms left water and colonized land. The skeleton in animals contributes to this support.

sections.heading: 16.1 HUMAN SKELETON
sections.title: 16.1 HUMAN SKELETON
sections.text: The vertebrate skeleton is composed either of cartilage or bone. Both tissues provide an internal supporting framework of the body. Human adults have bony skeleton, but cartilage is also present in some regions.

sections.heading: 16.1.1 Cartilage:
sections.title: 16.1.1 Cartilage:
sections.text:
Cartilage is a type of connective tissue consisting of cells called chondrocytes and a tough, flexible matrix made of type II collagen. Unlike other connective tissues, cartilage does not contain blood vessels and the chondrocytes are supplied by diffusion. Because of this, it heals very slowly.

Although the human skeleton is initially made up of cartilages and fibrous membranes, most of these early supports are soon replaced by bones. A few cartilages that remain in adults are found mainly in regions where flexible skeletal support is needed. There are three types of cartilage tissue in human body: hyaline, elastic, and fibrocartilage.

sections.heading: 16.1.2 Bone
sections.title: 16.1.2 Bone
sections.text:
Bone is a rigid form of connective tissue, which forms the endoskeleton of vertebrates. Bone is a living hard (resists compression) and strong (resists bending) structure. It consists of a hard ground substance or matrix and cells. In the adult human, the matrix consists of about 65% inorganic matter (calcium phosphate, carbonate etc) and about 35% organic substances (protein, collagen). The cells are embedded in the matrix.

The structure of bone is specially designed to withstand the compression strains falling upon it and to resist pressure. Bones are composed of cells for example; osteoblasts (cells that help form bone), and osteoclasts (cells that help eat away old bone).

Fig: 16.1 Different types of bone cells.

In addition, bone contains cells called osteocytes, which are mature osteoblasts that have ended their bone-forming capacity. These cells engage in metabolic exchange with the blood that flows through the bones.

Osteoblasts:

The osteoblasts are mononucleate cells. Osteoblasts produce a matrix which is composed mainly of Type I collagen. They are also responsible for mineralization of this matrix. Osteoblasts are the immature bone cells, and eventually become entrapped in the bone matrix to become osteocytes- the mature bone cell.

Osteocytes:

They are mature bone cells. They cease to generate mineralized matrix. Osteocytes have many extensions that reach out to meet osteoblasts and other osteocytes for the purposes of communication. They are responsible for the maintenance of bone and calcium. They also regulate the bone's response to stress and mechanical load.

Osteoclast:

Osteoclasts are large, multinucleated cells that remove bone tissue by removing its mineralized matrix and breaking up the organic bone. This process is known as bone resorption. They are equipped with phagocytic-like mechanisms similar to circulating macrophages.

Composition of Bone

Bone is a dynamic tissue that is being reshaped by the activity of osteoclasts and osteoblasts. Cells are embedded in a firm calcified matrix. 30% matrix is composed of organic material, chiefly of collagen fibers (90%) and glycoproteins. 70% matrix is composed of inorganic salts. The chief inorganic constituent of bone is needle like crystals of hydroxyapatite, a form of calcium phosphate. Sodium, magnesium, potassium, chloride, fluoride, bicarbonate and citrate ions are also present in variable amounts. Calcium and phosphate may be released into the blood as needed, under the control of two hormones, parathormone and calcitonin.

Table: 16.1 Comparison between bone and cartilage

BONE | CARTILAGE
(i) Mature cells are osteocytes. | (i) Mature cells are chondrocytes
(ii) Bone matrix contains type I collagen. | (ii) Cartilages mostly contain type II collagen
(iii) Strengthen by inorganic calcium salts. | (iii) No inorganic salts
(iv) Bones are constantly reshaped by osteoblasts, and osteoclasts. | (iv) Cartilages are not reshaped
(v) Bones have rich blood supply. | (v) No blood circulation in cartilages

sections.heading: 16.1.3 Main divisions of human skeleton
sections.title: 16.1.3 Main divisions of human skeleton
sections.headingPashto: د انسان د اسکلېټ اصلي برخې
sections.text:
A skeleton of cartilage supports human body, but by the time of birth much of the cartilage had been transformed into 350 bones. As one grows many of these bones fuse with one another so that at adult stage, skeleton consists of 206 individual bones which are grouped into two general divisions; axial skeleton, the basic framework of the body and appendicular skeleton, the extremities. Axial skeleton consists of skull, vertebrae and ribs. Appendicular skeleton includes pectoral girdle with forelimbs and pelvic girdle with hind limbs. Numbers and distribution of bones in human body is given in the table 16.2.

Fig: 16.2 Human Skeleton

Table: 16.2 Distribution of bones in human body.

Main part | Subdivision | Bones | Total bones
Skull | Cranium | 8 bones | 28
 | Ears | 6 bones | 
 | Face | 14 bones | 
Neck | Hyoid | bone 1 | 1
Trunk | Vertebral column | 26 bones | 51
 | Chest bone | 1 | 
 | Ribs | 24 bones | 
Limbs | Upper limbs | 64 | 126
 | Lower limb | 62 | 

Table: 16.3 The 28 bones of the skull are tabulated here.

Skull | Unpaired bones | Paired bones
Cranium 8 bones | Frontal, Occipital, Sphenoid, Ethmoid | Parietal, Temporal
Facial bones (face) 14 bones | Mandible, Vomer | Maxilla, Zygomatic, Lacrimal, Nasal, Inferior concha, Palatine
Auditory ossicle (ear bones) 6 bones |  | Malleus, Incus, Stapes

paras.urdu: غضروف کا ڈھانچا انسانی جسم کو سہارا دیتا ہے، لیکن پیدائش تک زیادہ تر غضروف 350 ہڈیوں میں بدل چکا ہوتا ہے۔ نشوونما کے ساتھ کئی ہڈیاں آپس میں جڑ جاتی ہیں، اس لیے بالغ ڈھانچا 206 الگ ہڈیوں پر مشتمل ہوتا ہے؛ یہ دو حصوں میں تقسیم ہیں: محوری ڈھانچا، جسم کا بنیادی فریم، اور ضمیمی ڈھانچا، اطراف کے اعضا۔ محوری ڈھانچا کھوپڑی، مہروں اور پسلیوں پر مشتمل ہے۔ ضمیمی ڈھانچے میں اگلے اعضا کے ساتھ کندھوں کی پٹی اور پچھلے اعضا کے ساتھ شرونی پٹی شامل ہیں۔ انسانی جسم کی ہڈیوں کی تعداد اور تقسیم جدول 16.2 میں دی گئی ہے۔
paras.pashto: د غضروف اسکلېټ د انسان بدن ملاتړ کوي، خو د زېږون تر وخته د غضروف ډېره برخه په 350 هډوکو بدله شوې وي. د ودې پر مهال ډېر هډوکي سره یوځای کېږي، نو په بلوغ کې اسکلېټ 206 جلا هډوکي لري؛ دا په دوو برخو وېشل کېږي: محوري اسکلېټ، د بدن بنسټیز چوکاټ، او ضمیموي اسکلېټ، اندامونه. محوري اسکلېټ له کوپړۍ، مهرو او پښتيو جوړ دی. ضمیموي اسکلېټ د مخکنیو اندامونو سره صدري کمربند او د شاتنیو اندامونو سره حوضي کمربند لري. د انسان په بدن کې د هډوکو شمېر او وېش په 16.2 جدول کې ورکړل شوی دی.

sections.heading: Axial Skeleton
sections.title: Axial Skeleton
sections.text:
Axial skeleton consists of skull, vertebral column and ribs.

1. Skull The skull consists of cranium (or facial bones), ear bone (or auditory ossicles) and hyoid bone. The primary function of skull is the protection of brain. The human skull is composed of 22 bones, besides 6 tiny ear bones and one hyoid bone.

At the time of birth several of the bones of the cranium are not completely formed. If the bones of cranium were completely formed at the time of birth, great difficultly would have been experienced in the birth canal.

Fig: 16.3 Major bones of human skull.

2. Vertebral Column

The vertebral column forms a more or less rigid rod. It extends through the length of the trunk on the dorsal side and form the backbone. It houses and protects the spinal cord. It is a place of attachment of pelvic and pectoral girdle.

In man, there are 33 vertebrae. Seven cervical vertebrae in the neck region; in the thorax region 12 thoracic vertebrae; in the lower back region 5 lumber vertebrae; in the sacral region 5 sacral vertebrae (to which the pelvic girdle is attached) and at the end of the vertebral column is the coccyx or tail bone which consists of 4 small fused vertebrae. The coccyx is man's vestige of a tail.

Fig: 16.4 Vertebral column of the human skeleton (side view)

3. Ribs

In man there are twelve pairs of ribs, one pair articulating with each of the thoracic vertebrae forming a cage that encloses the heart and lungs. Ten pairs of ribs are connected anteriorly with the sternum. Seven pairs out of these ten pairs are directly connected with the sternum and are known as 'true ribs', while the other three pairs are indirectly connected with the sternum through the costal arch and are known as 'false ribs'. The lower two pairs of ribs are not attached in front and are known as the "floating ribs".

Fig: 16.5 Human Ribs

paras.pashto: په انسان کې 33 مهرې شته. په غاړه کې 7 عنقي، په سینه کې 12 صدري، د ملا په لاندې برخه کې 5 قطني، په سکرل سیمه کې 5 سکرل مهرې (چې حوضي کمربند ورسره نښتی دی) شته؛ په پای کې کوکسیکس یا د لکۍ هډوکی له 4 وړو یوځای شوو مهرو جوړ دی. کوکسیکس په انسان کې د لکۍ پاتې شونی دی.

paras.text: 3. Ribs
paras.urdu: 3۔ پسلیاں
paras.pashto: 3. پښتۍ

paras.text: In man there are twelve pairs of ribs, one pair articulating with each of the thoracic vertebrae forming a cage that encloses the heart and lungs. Ten pairs of ribs are connected anteriorly with the sternum. Seven pairs out of these ten pairs are directly connected with the sternum and are known as 'true ribs', while the other three pairs are indirectly connected with the sternum through the costal arch and are known as 'false ribs'. The lower two pairs of ribs are not attached in front and are known as the "floating ribs".
paras.urdu: انسان میں پسلیوں کے بارہ جوڑے ہیں؛ ہر صدری مہرے سے ایک جوڑا جڑ کر دل اور پھیپھڑوں کے گرد پنجرہ بناتا ہے۔ پسلیوں کے دس جوڑے سامنے سینے کی ہڈی سے جڑے ہیں۔ ان دس میں سات جوڑے براہِ راست سینے کی ہڈی سے جڑے اور حقیقی پسلیاں کہلاتے ہیں؛ باقی تین پسلیوں کی محراب سے بالواسطہ جڑے اور کاذب پسلیاں کہلاتے ہیں۔ نچلے دو جوڑے سامنے نہیں جڑے ہوتے اور تیرتی پسلیاں کہلاتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: په انسان کې د پښتيو دولس جوړې دي؛ له هرې صدري مهرې سره یوه جوړه نښلي او د زړه او سږو شاوخوا قفس جوړوي. د پښتيو لس جوړې له مخې د سینې له هډوکي سره نښتې دي. له دغو لسو جوړو اووه نېغ د سینې له هډوکي سره نښتې او ریښتینې پښتۍ بلل کېږي؛ نورې درې د پښتۍ د قوس له لارې په غیر مستقیم ډول نښتې او کاذبې پښتۍ بلل کېږي. لاندې دوه جوړې له مخې نه دي نښتې او ازادې پښتۍ بلل کېږي.

sections.heading: Appendicular Skeleton
sections.title: Appendicular Skeleton
sections.text:
The appendicular skeleton consists of pectoral girdles with forelimbs and pelvic girdle with hind limbs.

Pectoral Girdle

The bones of the pectoral girdle consists of a ventral coracoid, which meets the sternum medially; a scapula, extending dorsally; and a clavicle, which lies on the ventral side between the scapula and sternum and anterior to the coracoid.

Forelimbs

The forelimbs consist of a humerus in the upper arm region; a radius and an ulna in the lower arm region; 8 carpels in the wrist and 5 metacarpels in the palm of the hand and 14 phalanges.

Pelvic Girdle

Hind limbs are attached to the vertebral column through pelvic girdle, which is made of two coxal bones. Each of these bones are found by the combination of three bones; ischium, illium and pubis.

Hind limbs

Each hind limb consists of thigh, shank, ankle and foot. In the hind limb there is a single femur in the thigh, a pair of bones, the tibia and fibula, in the shank, 8 anklebones, followed by five longer metatarsals in the foot and finally five rows of fourteen phalanges in the toe.

sections.heading: 16.1.4 Joints
sections.title: 16.1.4 Joints
sections.text:
The sites where two or more bones meet are called joints or articulations. Joints have two fundamental functions: they give mobility to the skeleton and hold the skeletal parts together.

Structural classification of joints

Structural classification of joints is based on the material binding the bones together and whether or not a joint cavity is present. There are three types of joints, the fibrous, cartilaginous, and synovial joints.

1. Fibrous joints:

In fibrous joints, a thin layer of fibrous connective tissue holds the bones firmly in position. There is no joint cavity between the bones. In general fibrous joints are immovable. These joints provide strength and support for the body, and have protective role for the delicate structures. Fibrous joints are formed between the bones of skull, between sacrum and iliac of pelvic girdles, and between the bones of pelvic girdle.

Fig: 16.6 Fibrous joints in skull.

ii. Cartilaginous joints:

Cartilaginous joints are connected entirely by fibrocartilage or hyaline cartilage. Joint cavity is absent. Bones can glide over each other to a limited extent. Cartilage forms a flexible connection so that these joints allow slight movement. Such joints are formed between vertebrae, and between wrist and ankle bones.

Fig: 16.7 Cartilaginous joints in vertebral column.

Synovial joints:

Synovial joints are those in which the articulating bones are separated by a fluid-containing joint cavity (synovial cavity). This arrangement permits freedom of movement, and all synovial joints are freely movable.

Synovial joints are reinforced and strengthened by a number of bandlike ligaments. These ligaments hold the bones in position. Based on the shape of their articular surfaces, the synovial joints have different structural plan. This structural plan determines the type of movement allowed.

Fig: 16.8 Hinge joint between trochlea of humerus and trochlear notch of ulna at the elbow.

Fig: 16.9 Ball-and-socket joint between head of the femur and acetabulum of the hip bone.

The synovial joints can be classified into two major categories; hinge and ball and socket joints.

Hinge joints:

In hinge joints, a cylindrical projection of one bone fits into a trough-shaped surface on another. These joints permit movement in one plane that is, permit flexion and extension only. Hinge joints are capable of bearing heavy loads. Examples are elbow and knee joint.

Ball-and-Socket Joints:

In ball-and-socket joints the spherical or hemispherical head of one bone articulates with the cuplike socket of another. These joints are the most freely moving synovial joints. The shoulder and hip joints are examples.

sections.heading: 16.2.1 Disorders of human skeleton:
sections.title: 16.2.1 Disorders of human skeleton:
sections.text:
16.2 DISORDERS OF SKELETON

Although human skeleton is hard and strong, yet deformities do occur resulting in reduced movement or complete immobility. Deformities of skeleton may be genetic, hormonal or due to the effects of nutrient deficiency

Disc slip:

The discs are protective shock-absorbing pads between the bones of the spine (vertebrae). The discs of the spine are also referred to as intervertebral discs. Although they do not actually "slip," a disc may split or rupture. This can cause the disc cartilage and nearby tissue to fail (herniate), allowing the inner gel portion of the disc to escape into the surrounding tissue. This leaking jelly-like substance can place pressure on the spinal cord or on an adjacent nerve to cause symptoms of pain either around the damaged disc or anywhere along the area controlled by that nerve. This condition is also known as a herniated disc. The most frequently affected area is the lower back, but any disk can rupture, including those in the neck.

Factors that lead to a slipped disc include aging with associated degeneration and loss of elasticity of the discs and supporting structures; injury from improper lifting, especially if accompanied by twisting or turning; and excessive strain forces associated with physical activities.

Spondylosis:

Spondylosis (spinal osteoarthritis) is a degenerative disorder that may cause loss of normal spinal structure and function. Although aging is the primary cause, the location and rate of degeneration is individual.

The degenerative process of spondylosis may affect the cervical (neck), thoracic (mid-back), or lumbar (lower back) regions of the spine.

Fig: 1610 Spondylosis.

Sciatica:

Sciatica refers to pain, weakness, numbness, or tingling in the leg. It is caused by injury to or pressure on the sciatic nerve. This nerve starts in the lower spine and runs down the back of each leg. Common causes of sciatica include: Slipped disc, piriformis syndrome (a pain disorder involving the narrow muscle in the buttock), pelvic injury or fracture and tumors.

Arthritis:

The arthritis is joint inflammation and it can affect joints in any part of the body. Arthritis is the leading cause of disability in those over the age of 65. Some of the symptoms of arthritis are:

Joint pain and swelling.
Stiffness particularly in the mornings.
The feeling of warmth around a joint.
Redness of skin around the joint.
Inability to move the joint easily.

Some of the causes of arthritis are broken bone, infection in the area, an autoimmune disease and general wear and tear on joints.

paras.text: The discs are protective shock-absorbing pads between the bones of the spine (vertebrae). The discs of the spine are also referred to as intervertebral discs. Although they do not actually "slip," a disc may split or rupture. This can cause the disc cartilage and nearby tissue to fail (herniate), allowing the inner gel portion of the disc to escape into the surrounding tissue. This leaking jelly-like substance can place pressure on the spinal cord or on an adjacent nerve to cause symptoms of pain either around the damaged disc or anywhere along the area controlled by that nerve. This condition is also known as a herniated disc. The most frequently affected area is the lower back, but any disk can rupture, including those in the neck.
paras.urdu: ڈسکس ریڑھ کی ہڈی کے مہروں کے درمیان حفاظتی، صدمہ جذب کرنے والی گدیاں ہیں۔ ریڑھ کی ڈسکس بین المہری ڈسکس بھی کہلاتی ہیں۔ اگرچہ یہ حقیقت میں سرکتی نہیں، ڈسک پھٹ یا شق ہو سکتی ہے۔ اس سے ڈسک کا غضروف اور قریبی بافت کمزور ہو کر باہر ابھر سکتے ہیں، اور اندر کا جیل آس پاس کے بافت میں نکل سکتا ہے۔ نکلنے والا جیلی نما مادہ حرام مغز یا قریبی عصب پر دباؤ ڈال کر خراب ڈسک کے آس پاس یا اس عصب کے زیرکنٹرول علاقے میں درد پیدا کر سکتا ہے۔ اس حالت کو ہرنی ایٹڈ ڈسک بھی کہتے ہیں۔ زیادہ تر کمر کا نچلا حصہ متاثر ہوتا ہے، مگر گردن سمیت کوئی بھی ڈسک پھٹ سکتی ہے۔

paras.text: Factors that lead to a slipped disc include aging with associated degeneration and loss of elasticity of the discs and supporting structures; injury from improper lifting, especially if accompanied by twisting or turning; and excessive strain forces associated with physical activities.

paras.text: Spondylosis (spinal osteoarthritis) is a degenerative disorder that may cause loss of normal spinal structure and function. Although aging is the primary cause, the location and rate of degeneration is individual.

paras.text: Sciatica refers to pain, weakness, numbness, or tingling in the leg. It is caused by injury to or pressure on the sciatic nerve. This nerve starts in the lower spine and runs down the back of each leg. Common causes of sciatica include: Slipped disc, piriformis syndrome (a pain disorder involving the narrow muscle in the buttock), pelvic injury or fracture and tumors.

sections.heading: 16.2.2 Bone fractures
sections.title: 16.2.2 Bone fractures
sections.text:
A fracture is the medical term for a broken bone. They occur when the physical force exerted on the bone is stronger than the bone itself. So bones break when they cannot withstand a force or trauma applied to them.

Simple fracture: Closed (simple) fractures are those in which the skin is intact.
Compound fracture: The fracture is an open (compound) fracture if the bone ends penetrate the skin and form a wound.

Repair of a fractured bone:

A fracture is treated by reduction, the realignment of the broken bone ends. In closed or external reduction, the bone ends are coaxed into position by the physician's hands. In open (internal) reduction, the bone ends are secured together surgically with pins or wires. After the broken bone is reduced, it is immobilized by a cast to allow the healing process to begin. For a simple fracture the healing time is six to eight weeks for small or medium-sized bones in young adults, but it is much longer for large, weight-bearing bones and for bones of elderly people (because of their poorer circulation). Repair in a simple fracture involves four major stages;

Hematoma formation: When a bone breaks, blood vessels in the bone, and perhaps in surrounding tissues, are torn and hemorrhage occur. As a result, a hematoma, a mass of clotted blood, forms at the fracture site. Soon, bone cells deprived of nutrition die, and the tissue at the site becomes swollen, painful, and inflamed.
Fibrocartilaginous callus formation: Within a few days, several events lead to the formation of soft granulation tissue, also called the soft callus. Capillaries grow into the hematoma and phagocytic cells invade the area and begin cleaning up the debris. Meanwhile, fibroblasts and osteoblasts invade the fracture site and begin reconstructing the bone.

The fibroblasts produce collagen fibers that span the break and connect the broken bone ends, and some differentiate into chondroblasts that secrete cartilage matrix.

Fig: 16.11 Steps in the repair of fractured bone.

Within this mass of repair tissue, osteoblasts begin forming spongy bone, but those farthest from the capillary supply secrete an externally bulging cartilaginous matrix that later calcifies. This entire mass of repair tissue, now called the fibrocartilaginous callus, splints the broken bone.

Bony callus formation: Within a week the fibrocartilaginous callus is gradually converted to a bony (hard) callus of spongy bone. Bony callus formation continues until a firm union is formed about two months later.
Bone remodeling: Beginning during bony callus formation and continuing for several months after, the bony callus is remodeled. The compact bone is laid down to reconstruct the shaft walls. The final structure of the remodeled area resembles that of the original unbroken bony region because it responds to the same set of mechanical stressors.

For a simple fracture the healing time is six to eight weeks for small or medium-sized bones in young adults, but it is much longer for large, weight-bearing bones and for bones of elderly people (because of their poorer circulation). Repair in a simple fracture involves four major stages;
paras.urdu: فریکچر کا علاج ریڈکشن، یعنی ٹوٹی ہڈی کے سروں کو درست صف میں لانے، سے ہوتا ہے۔ بند یا بیرونی ریڈکشن میں معالج ہاتھوں سے ہڈی کے سرے اپنی جگہ لاتا ہے۔ کھلے یا اندرونی ریڈکشن میں جراحی سے پنوں یا تاروں کے ذریعے ہڈی کے سرے جوڑے جاتے ہیں۔ ہڈی درست کرنے کے بعد پلاسٹر سے اسے غیر متحرک کیا جاتا ہے تاکہ مندمل ہونے کا عمل شروع ہو۔ نوجوان بالغوں کی چھوٹی یا درمیانی ہڈیوں کا سادہ فریکچر چھ سے آٹھ ہفتوں میں مندمل ہوتا ہے؛ بڑی وزن اٹھانے والی ہڈیوں اور بوڑھوں کی ہڈیوں میں، کمزور دورانِ خون کے سبب، زیادہ وقت لگتا ہے۔ سادہ فریکچر کی مرمت کے چار اہم مرحلے ہیں:
paras.pashto: د ماتېدنې درملنه په رېډکشن، یعنې د مات هډوکي د سرونو په بیا سم برابرولو، کېږي. په تړلي یا بهرني رېډکشن کې ډاکټر په لاسونو د هډوکي سرونه خپل ځای ته برابروي. په پرانیستي یا داخلي رېډکشن کې د هډوکي سرونه په جراحي ډول په مېخونو یا سیمونو سره ټینګېږي. د مات هډوکي تر برابرولو وروسته په ګچ بې حرکته کېږي څو د رغېدو بهیر پیل شي. په ځوانو بالغو کې د وړو یا منځنیو هډوکو ساده ماتېدنه له شپږو تر اتو اوونیو رغېږي؛ خو د لویو وزن وړونکو هډوکو او د زړو خلکو د هډوکو لپاره، د کمزوري دوران له امله، ډېر وخت غواړي. د ساده ماتېدنې ترمیم څلور مهم پړاوونه لري:

paras.text: Hematoma formation: When a bone breaks, blood vessels in the bone, and perhaps in surrounding tissues, are torn and hemorrhage occur. As a result, a hematoma, a mass of clotted blood, forms at the fracture site. Soon, bone cells deprived of nutrition die, and the tissue at the site becomes swollen, painful, and inflamed.
paras.urdu: ہیماٹوما بننا: ہڈی ٹوٹنے سے اس کی اور ممکنہ طور پر آس پاس کے بافتوں کی خون کی نالیاں پھٹتی ہیں اور خون بہتا ہے۔ نتیجتاً فریکچر کی جگہ جمے خون کا ڈھیر، ہیماٹوما، بنتا ہے۔ جلد غذائیت سے محروم ہڈی کے خلیے مر جاتے ہیں اور مقامی بافت سوجن، درد اور سوزش کا شکار ہوتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: د هیماتوما جوړېدل: د هډوکي په ماتېدو په هډوکي او ښايي شاوخوا نسجونو کې د وینې رګونه څېرېږي او وینه بهېږي. په پایله کې د ماتېدنې په ځای کې د ټینګې شوې وینې کتله، هیماتوما، جوړېږي. ژر له غذا محروم هډوکین حجرې مري او د ځای نسج پړسېږي، دردناک او ملتهب کېږي.

paras.text: Fibrocartilaginous callus formation: Within a few days, several events lead to the formation of soft granulation tissue, also called the soft callus. Capillaries grow into the hematoma and phagocytic cells invade the area and begin cleaning up the debris. Meanwhile, fibroblasts and osteoblasts invade the fracture site and begin reconstructing the bone.
paras.urdu: ریشے دار غضروفی کالس بننا: چند دنوں میں کئی واقعات نرم دانے دار بافت بناتے ہیں، جسے نرم کالس بھی کہتے ہیں۔ ہیماٹوما میں باریک نالیاں بڑھتی ہیں اور فاگوسائٹک خلیے داخل ہو کر ملبہ صاف کرنے لگتے ہیں۔ اس دوران فائبروبلاسٹس اور اوسٹیوبلاسٹس فریکچر کی جگہ پہنچ کر ہڈی دوبارہ بناتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د فایبروغضروفي کالس جوړېدل: په څو ورځو کې ګڼې پېښې نرم ګرانولېشن نسج جوړوي، چې نرم کالس هم بلل کېږي. شعریه رګونه هیماتوما ته وده کوي او فاګوسایټیک حجرې سیمې ته ننوځي او پاتې شوني پاکوي. په همدې وخت کې فایبروبلاسټونه او اوستیوبلاسټونه د ماتېدنې ځای ته ننوځي او د هډوکي بیا جوړول پیلوي.

paras.text: The fibroblasts produce collagen fibers that span the break and connect the broken bone ends, and some differentiate into chondroblasts that secrete cartilage matrix.
paras.urdu: فائبروبلاسٹس کولیجن ریشے بناتے ہیں جو دراڑ پار کرکے ٹوٹے سروں کو ملاتے ہیں؛ کچھ کونڈروبلاسٹس بن کر غضروفی میٹرکس خارج کرتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: فایبروبلاسټونه د کولاژن ریشې جوړوي چې د ماتېدنې تشه نښلوي او مات سرونه سره تړي؛ ځینې په کونډروبلاسټونو بدلېږي او غضروفي ماتریکس ترشح کوي.

paras.text: Fig: 16.11 Steps in the repair of fractured bone.
paras.urdu: شکل 16.11: ٹوٹی ہوئی ہڈی کی مرمت کے مراحل
paras.pashto: شکل 16.11: د مات هډوکي د ترمیم پړاوونه

paras.text: Within this mass of repair tissue, osteoblasts begin forming spongy bone, but those farthest from the capillary supply secrete an externally bulging cartilaginous matrix that later calcifies. This entire mass of repair tissue, now called the fibrocartilaginous callus, splints the broken bone.
paras.urdu: اس مرمتی بافت میں اوسٹیوبلاسٹس مسام دار ہڈی بناتے ہیں، مگر باریک نالیوں سے دور والے باہر ابھرا غضروفی میٹرکس خارج کرتے ہیں جو بعد میں کیلشیائی ہوتا ہے۔ مرمتی بافت کی یہ پوری کمیت، اب ریشے دار غضروفی کالس، ٹوٹی ہڈی کو سہارا دیتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: د ترمیم په دې نسج کې اوستیوبلاسټونه اسفنجي هډوکی جوړوي، خو له شعریه رسونې ډېر لرې حجرې بهر ته راوتونکی غضروفي ماتریکس ترشح کوي چې وروسته کلسیفای کېږي. د ترمیم د نسج دا ټوله کتله، چې اوس فایبروغضروفي کالس بلل کېږي، مات هډوکی ټینګ ساتي.

paras.text: Bony callus formation: Within a week the fibrocartilaginous callus is gradually converted to a bony (hard) callus of spongy bone. Bony callus formation continues until a firm union is formed about two months later.
paras.urdu: ہڈی کا کالس بننا: ایک ہفتے کے اندر ریشے دار غضروفی کالس بتدریج مسام دار ہڈی کے سخت کالس میں بدلتا ہے۔ ہڈی کا کالس بننا تقریباً دو ماہ بعد مضبوط جوڑ بننے تک جاری رہتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: د هډوکین کالس جوړېدل: په یوه اوونۍ کې فایبروغضروفي کالس ورو ورو د اسفنجي هډوکي په کلک کالس بدلېږي. د هډوکین کالس جوړېدل تر هغه دوام کوي چې نږدې دوه میاشتې وروسته ټینګ اتصال جوړ شي.

paras.text: Bone remodeling: Beginning during bony callus formation and continuing for several months after, the bony callus is remodeled. The compact bone is laid down to reconstruct the shaft walls. The final structure of the remodeled area resembles that of the original unbroken bony region because it responds to the same set of mechanical stressors.
paras.urdu: ہڈی کی نئی تشکیل: ہڈی کے کالس بننے کے دوران شروع ہو کر کئی ماہ بعد تک اس کی نئی تشکیل جاری رہتی ہے۔ ہڈی کے درمیانی حصے کی دیواریں دوبارہ بنانے کے لیے ٹھوس ہڈی جمع ہوتی ہے۔ دوبارہ بنے حصے کی آخری ساخت اصل سالم ہڈی جیسی ہوتی ہے کیونکہ وہ انہی میکانی دباؤوں کا ردعمل دیتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: د هډوکي بیا بڼه جوړول: د هډوکین کالس د جوړېدو پر مهال پیلېږي او څو میاشتې وروسته هم د کالس بیا بڼه جوړېږي. د هډوکي د منځنۍ برخې د دېوالونو د بیا جوړولو لپاره متراکم هډوکی اېښودل کېږي. د بیا جوړې شوې سیمې وروستی جوړښت اصلي روغ هډوکي ته ورته وي، ځکه هماغو میخانیکي فشارونو ته غبرګون ښيي.

sections.heading: 16.2.3 Joint injuries:
sections.title: 16.2.3 Joint injuries:
sections.text:
Joint dislocation:

A dislocated joint is a joint that slips out of place. It occurs when the ends of bones are forced away from their normal positions. When a joint is dislocated, it no longer functions properly. A severe dislocation can cause tearing of the muscles, ligaments and tendons that support the joint. Symptoms include; swelling, intense Pain, and immobility of the affected joint. The most common causes are a blow, fall, or other trauma to the joint. In some cases, dislocations are caused by a disease or a defective ligament.

Rheumatoid arthritis can also cause joint dislocation. A dislocated joint usually can only be successfully 'reduced' into its normal position by a trained medical professional. Surgery may be needed to repair or tighten stretched ligaments.

Sprain:

A sprain is an injury to a ligament. Commonly injured ligaments are in the ankle, knee, and wrist. The ligaments can be injured by being stretched too far from their normal position.

Fig: 16.12 Ligaments in the ankle.

The ligaments are to hold skeleton together in a normal alignment so ligaments prevent abnormal movements. However, when too much force is applied to a ligament, such as in a fall, the ligaments can be stretched or torn. The sprain should be rested. Sprains can be usually treated with treatments such as icing and physical therapy. Dressings, bandages, or ace-wraps should be used to immobilize the sprain and provide support.

The most distinguishing functional characteristic of muscles is their ability to transform chemical energy (ATP) into mechanical energy. In doing so, they become capable of exerting force.

sections.heading: 16.3.1 Types of muscles
sections.title: 16.3.1 Types of muscles
sections.text:
Based on their location, three types of muscles are skeletal, cardiac, and smooth.

i. Skeletal Muscles

Skeletal muscles are attached to and cover the bony skeleton. Skeletal muscle fibers are multinucleated, the longest muscle cells having obvious stripes called striations and are under voluntary control. They can contract rapidly, but get tire easily and must rest after short periods of activity, or fatigued. Nevertheless, it can exert tremendous power.

Skeletal muscles are also remarkably adaptable. For example, hand muscles can exert a force of a fraction of an ounce to pick up a dropped paper clip and the same muscles can exert a force of many pounds to pick heavy loads like a bucket full of water. Skeletal muscles are primarily involved in locomotory actions and changes of body postures.

Fig: 16.13 Structure of skeletal muscle.

ii. Cardiac Muscles

Cardiac muscles occur only in the heart where they constitute the bulk of the heart walls. Cardiac muscle cells are arranged in a characteristic branching pattern. Like skeletal muscle cells, cardiac muscle cells are striated, but are involuntary and have single nucleus.

Cardiac muscles usually contract at a fairly steady rate set by the heart’s pacemaker, but neural controls allow the heart to “shift into high gear” for brief periods. Rhythmic contraction of cardiac muscles in atria and ventricles of the heart pump blood throughout the body.

Fig: 16.14 Structure of cardiac muscle

iii. Smooth Muscles

Smooth muscles are found in the walls of hollow visceral organs, such as the stomach, urinary bladder, respiratory passages, and blood vessels. Smooth muscle cells are spindle shaped. They have one centrally placed nucleus per cell. They have no striations, and are not subjected to voluntary control.

Fig: 16.15 Structure of smooth muscle.

paras.pashto: ii. قلبي عضلې

paras.text: Cardiac muscles occur only in the heart where they constitute the bulk of the heart walls. Cardiac muscle cells are arranged in a characteristic branching pattern. Like skeletal muscle cells, cardiac muscle cells are striated, but are involuntary and have single nucleus.
paras.urdu: قلبی عضلات صرف دل میں ہوتے ہیں اور اس کی دیواروں کا بڑا حصہ بناتے ہیں۔ قلبی عضلاتی خلیے خاص شاخ دار ترتیب رکھتے ہیں۔ ڈھانچائی خلیوں کی طرح قلبی عضلاتی خلیے دھاری دار ہیں، مگر غیر اختیاری اور ایک مرکزے والے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: قلبي عضلې یوازې په زړه کې وي او د زړه د دېوالونو ډېره برخه جوړوي. قلبي عضلاتي حجرې په ځانګړي ښاخ لرونکي ترتیب کې دي. د اسکلېټي حجرو په څېر قلبي عضلاتي حجرې پټې لري، خو غیر ارادي او یو هسته لرونکې دي.

paras.text: Cardiac muscles usually contract at a fairly steady rate set by the heart’s pacemaker, but neural controls allow the heart to “shift into high gear” for brief periods. Rhythmic contraction of cardiac muscles in atria and ventricles of the heart pump blood throughout the body.
paras.urdu: قلبی عضلات عموماً دل کے پیس میکر کی مقررہ تقریباً مستقل رفتار سے سکڑتے ہیں، مگر اعصابی کنٹرول مختصر مدت کے لیے دل کی رفتار بڑھا سکتا ہے۔ دل کے ایٹریا اور وینٹریکلز میں قلبی عضلات کا باقاعدہ سکڑاؤ پورے جسم میں خون پمپ کرتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: قلبي عضلې عموماً د زړه د پېس مېکر په ټاکلې نسبتاً ثابته کچه منقبضېږي، خو عصبي کنټرول زړه ته د لنډ وخت لپاره د چټک کار اجازه ورکوي. د زړه په دهلیزونو او بطینونو کې د قلبي عضلو منظم انقباض ټول بدن ته وینه پمپ کوي.

paras.text: iii. Smooth Muscles
paras.urdu: iii۔ ہموار عضلات
paras.pashto: iii. نرمې عضلې

paras.text: Smooth muscles are found in the walls of hollow visceral organs, such as the stomach, urinary bladder, respiratory passages, and blood vessels. Smooth muscle cells are spindle shaped. They have one centrally placed nucleus per cell. They have no striations, and are not subjected to voluntary control.
paras.urdu: ہموار عضلات معدے، مثانے، تنفسی راستوں اور خون کی نالیوں جیسے کھوکھلے اندرونی اعضا کی دیواروں میں ہوتے ہیں۔ ہموار عضلاتی خلیے تکلے کی شکل کے ہیں۔ ہر خلیے میں مرکز میں ایک مرکزہ ہوتا ہے۔ ان میں دھاریاں نہیں ہوتیں اور یہ اختیاری کنٹرول میں نہیں ہوتے۔
paras.pashto: نرمې عضلې د تشو داخلي غړو په دېوالونو کې وي، لکه معده، مثانه، تنفسي لارې او د وینې رګونه. د نرمو عضلو حجرې د دوک په بڼه دي. په هره حجره کې په منځ کې یوه هسته لري. پټې نه لري او تر ارادي کنټرول لاندې نه دي.

sections.heading: 16.3.2 Structure of Skeletal Muscles
sections.title: 16.3.2 Structure of Skeletal Muscles
sections.text:
The skeletal muscles are attached to the skeleton. The skeletal muscle consists of muscles bundle, which are further composed of huge elongated cells called muscles fibre. These muscles fibres are cylindrical, unbranched and with a diameter of 10–100 µm.

Each fibre consists of a semi fluid matrix, the sarcoplasm or cytoplasm, containing many nuclei and a large number of mitochondria. The nuclei are located near the periphery of each fibre.

Each fibre is surrounded by a membrane sarcolemma. The sarcolemma of muscle fibre cell penetrates deep into the cell to form hollow elongated tube, the transverse tubule, T-tubule. The lumen of which is continuous with the extracellular fluid. The T-tubule and terminal portion of the adjacent envelope of sarcoplasmic reticulum (a modified type of endoplasmic reticulum that store calcium) form triads at regular intervals along the length of the fibril.

The nerve impulse is carried through the T-tubule to the adjacent sarcoplasmic reticulum. Fibre may be red due to the presence of the myoglobin- an oxygen storing pigmented protein. It also contain large amount of stored glycogen.

Fig: 16.16 Section through a muscle fibre.

The sarcoplasm of the fibre contains many contractile elements called myofibrils, which are 1–2 µm in diameter. Each myofibril has alternate light and dark bands, which give the fibre its “striped” appearances. It is because of this, that the skeletal muscles are also called striated or striped muscles.

Myofibrils consist of smaller contractile units called sarcomere. In each sarcomere a series of dark and light bands are evident along the length of myofibril. The dark bands are A band (anisotropic) and the light band are I band (isotropic). Each A band has a lighter strip in its midsection called H-zone (hele for bright) which inturn is bisected by M-line (medial line). The I band have midline called Z-line (zwish meaning between). A sarcomere is the region of a myofibril between two successive Z-line. The region of myofibril is the sarcomere, which is the functional unit of the contraction process in the muscles.

Each myofilament is made up of central thick filament surrounded by thin filament, which are linked together by cross bridges. The thick filament contains a protein, myosin.

Fig: 16.17 Composition of sarcomere.

Thin filament is composed of a protein actin as its main component besides it also has tropomyosin and troponin proteins. The myosin and actin help in contraction of the muscles.

Thick filament has a tail terminating in two globular heads, which are also called as cross bridges and these link thin and thick filaments during contraction.

Muscles Contraction

Contractility or the ability to contract is a fundamental characteristic of living substance. It is essential to all kinds of movements, except growth and cytoplasmic streaming.

The currently popular model of muscle fiber contraction is called the sliding filament hypothesis proposed by H .E. Huxely and A. F. Huxely. They observed that when the muscle contracts, the thick and thin filaments of the muscles fibre slide past each other but are not changed in length.

According to this model, the release of calcium ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum causes a reorientation of certain components in the thin actin filaments, permitting them to bind with extensions (heads) from the thick myosin filaments.

Each myosin head then binds and splits an ATP molecule and the energy released powers the head forward to the next binding component on the actin filament.

Fig: 16.18 Each sarcomere has a series of dark and light bands which are evident along the length of each myofibril.

As this occurs, the actin filament moves one "notch" past the myosin filament. As long as calcium ions and ATP are available in the cytoplasm, the myosin heads continue to "crawl" along the actin filaments, thereby contracting the sarcomere and muscle.

Recovery: Muscle Fibre Relaxation

When the electrical impulses reaching a muscle fibre cease, the sarcoplasmic reticulum begins to re-accumulate the calcium ions by active transport. Once most of the calcium is sequestered in the sarcoplasmic reticulum sacs, which takes only milliseconds, the binding between the myosin heads and the actin filaments can no longer occur. As a result, the thick and thin filaments slide past one another, returning to their relaxed state of minimal overlap. The sarcomeres (and muscle fibres) once again achieve their maximal length and stretchability.

Control of Muscle Contraction

The contraction of a muscle fibre is normally an all-or-none phenomenon. Once it is stimulated, a muscle fibre will contract to a set length, regardless of intensity of the stimulus above the threshold level.

Fig: 16.19 Sarcomere exhibiting contraction movement.

The question then arises: If fibre contraction is an all-or-none phenomenon, how do we manage the fine control of muscular activity that permits us to lift a pencil on one occasion and a bowling ball on another?

Part of the answer has to do with the physical relationship between motor neurons and muscle fibres. The axon of a motor neuron has many branches, each branch terminating at a single muscle fibre. Thus, depending on how many branches it has, one neuron can stimulate several to many different muscle fibres. All the muscle fibres triggered by a single neuron contract simultaneously as a single motor unit. Since a particular muscle may consist of many motor units, the total amount of muscle contraction depends on the number of motor neurons conducting impulses to their motor units in the muscle. If many neurons carry impulses at once, many motor units within the muscle will contract. This causes a stronger over all contraction of the muscle than if only a few motor units are activated.

Energy of Muscle Contraction

Muscle contraction needs energy. The immediate source of energy for the muscle contraction is ATP, stored in the muscle cells. An enzyme ATPase, in the muscle cells breaks ATP to ADP, thus releasing energy for muscle contraction. But much part of the energy comes from carbohydrates or glucose, stored as glycogen in the muscle cells. When muscle contraction begins, glycogen is converted into glucose, which is then broken down to form ATP. The muscle contraction then uses this ATP.

We know that in violent exercise, such as running, much energy is needed. Is the normal rate of formation of ATP in muscles fibers adequate for this? Apparently not, but the muscles cells of all vertebrates have a reserve of high-energy phosphate compound, called phosphocreatin. During periods of intensive muscular activity, the phosphocreatin is broken into creatin and a high-energy phosphate group. This group then unites with ADP to form ATP.

Of the total energy expended in muscles contraction, only about 35% is utilized for the performance of work; the remaining is liberated in the form of heat, which is employed to maintain body temperature. In cold weather the production of heat can be increased through voluntary muscular activity (walking, rubbing hand together etc) or involuntary by shivering. Conversely, in warm weather, muscular activity is deliberately decreased to reduce heat production.

paras.urdu: مایوفائبرلز چھوٹی انقباضی اکائیوں، سارکومیئرز، سے بنتے ہیں۔ ہر سارکومیئر میں مایوفائبرل کی لمبائی میں گہری اور ہلکی پٹیوں کی ترتیب نمایاں ہے۔ گہری پٹیاں A بینڈ (این آئسوٹروپک) اور ہلکی پٹیاں I بینڈ (آئسوٹروپک) ہیں۔ ہر A بینڈ کے وسط میں ہلکی پٹی H-zone (hele بمعنی روشن) ہوتی ہے، جسے M-line (درمیانی لکیر) دو حصوں میں بانٹتی ہے۔ I بینڈ کی درمیانی لکیر Z-line (zwish بمعنی درمیان) کہلاتی ہے۔ سارکومیئر دو مسلسل Z لائنوں کے درمیان مایوفائبرل کا حصہ ہے۔ مایوفائبرل کا یہ حصہ سارکومیئر ہے، جو عضلات کے سکڑنے کی فعلی اکائی ہے۔

I بند منځنۍ کرښه لري چې Z-line (zwish د ترمنځ په معنا) بلل کېږي. سارکومیر د مایوفایبریل هغه برخه ده چې د دوو پرله پسې Z کرښو ترمنځ ده. د مایوفایبریل دا سیمه سارکومیر دی، چې په عضلو کې د انقباض فعاله واحد دی.

paras.text: Contractility or the ability to contract is a fundamental characteristic of living substance. It is essential to all kinds of movements, except growth and cytoplasmic streaming.
paras.urdu: سکڑنے کی صلاحیت زندہ مادے کی بنیادی خصوصیت ہے۔ نشوونما اور سائٹوپلازم کی روانی کے علاوہ ہر قسم کی حرکت کے لیے یہ ضروری ہے۔
paras.pashto: انقباض یا د راټولېدو وړتیا د ژوندي مادې بنسټیزه ځانګړنه ده. له ودې او د سایتوپلازم له بهېدو پرته د هر ډول حرکت لپاره دا اړینه ده.

paras.text: The currently popular model of muscle fiber contraction is called the sliding filament hypothesis proposed by H .E. Huxely and A. F. Huxely. They observed that when the muscle contracts, the thick and thin filaments of the muscles fibre slide past each other but are not changed in length.
paras.urdu: عضلاتی ریشے کے سکڑاؤ کا مقبول نمونہ سلائیڈنگ فلامنٹ مفروضہ ہے، جسے ایچ ای ہکسلے اور اے ایف ہکسلے نے پیش کیا۔ انہوں نے دیکھا کہ عضلہ سکڑنے پر موٹے اور باریک فلامنٹس ایک دوسرے کے پاس سے سرکتے ہیں مگر ان کی لمبائی نہیں بدلتی۔
paras.pashto: د عضلاتي ریشې د انقباض مشهور ماډل د ښویېدونکي فیلامنټ فرضیه ده، چې H. E. Huxley او A. F. Huxley وړاندې کړې ده. هغوی ولیدل چې د عضلې د انقباض پر مهال پنډ او نري فیلامنټونه د یو بل له څنګ ښویېږي، خو اوږدوالی یې نه بدلېږي.

paras.text: According to this model, the release of calcium ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum causes a reorientation of certain components in the thin actin filaments, permitting them to bind with extensions (heads) from the thick myosin filaments.
paras.urdu: اس نمونے کے مطابق سارکوپلازمک ریٹیکولم سے کیلشیم آئن نکلنے پر باریک ایکٹن فلامنٹس کے بعض اجزا کی ترتیب بدلتی ہے، جس سے وہ موٹے مایوسن فلامنٹس کے سروں سے جڑ سکتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د دې ماډل له مخې له سارکوپلازمي شبکې د کلسیم ایونونو خوشې کېدل په نریو اکټین فیلامنټونو کې د ځینو برخو ترتیب بدلوي، څو د پنډو مایوسین فیلامنټونو له سرونو سره ونښلي.

paras.text: Each myosin head then binds and splits an ATP molecule and the energy released powers the head forward to the next binding component on the actin filament.
paras.urdu: پھر ہر مایوسن سر ATP سالمہ باندھ کر توڑتا ہے اور خارج شدہ توانائی سر کو ایکٹن کے اگلے اتصال تک آگے بڑھاتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: بیا هر مایوسین سر د ATP مالیکول نښلوي او ماتوي، او خوشې شوې انرژي سر د اکټین پر فیلامنټ بل نښلېدونکي ځای ته وړاندې وړي.

paras.text: As this occurs, the actin filament moves one "notch" past the myosin filament. As long as calcium ions and ATP are available in the cytoplasm, the myosin heads continue to "crawl" along the actin filaments, thereby contracting the sarcomere and muscle.

paras.text: Recovery: Muscle Fibre Relaxation
paras.urdu: بحالی: عضلاتی ریشے کا ڈھیلا ہونا
paras.pashto: بېرته رغېدل: د عضلاتي ریشې استرخا

paras.text: When the electrical impulses reaching a muscle fibre cease, the sarcoplasmic reticulum begins to re-accumulate the calcium ions by active transport. Once most of the calcium is sequestered in the sarcoplasmic reticulum sacs, which takes only milliseconds, the binding between the myosin heads and the actin filaments can no longer occur. As a result, the thick and thin filaments slide past one another, returning to their relaxed state of minimal overlap. The sarcomeres (and muscle fibres) once again achieve their maximal length and stretchability.
paras.urdu: عضلاتی ریشے تک برقی پیغامات رکنے پر سارکوپلازمک ریٹیکولم فعال منتقلی سے کیلشیم آئن دوبارہ جمع کرتا ہے۔ زیادہ تر کیلشیم چند ملی سیکنڈ میں سارکوپلازمک ریٹیکولم کی تھیلیوں میں جمع ہو جائے تو مایوسن سروں اور ایکٹن کا اتصال مزید نہیں ہو سکتا۔ نتیجتاً موٹے اور باریک فلامنٹس سرک کر کم سے کم تداخل کی آرام حالت میں واپس آتے ہیں۔ سارکومیئرز اور عضلاتی ریشے دوبارہ زیادہ سے زیادہ لمبائی اور کھنچنے کی صلاحیت حاصل کرتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: کله چې عضلاتي ریشې ته رسېدونکي برېښنايي پیغامونه بند شي، سارکوپلازمي شبکه په فعال لېږد د کلسیم ایونونه بیا راټولوي. کله چې ډېری کلسیم په څو ملي ثانیو کې د سارکوپلازمي شبکې په کڅوړو کې وساتل شي، د مایوسین د سرونو او اکټین ترمنځ نښلېدل نور نه کېږي. په پایله کې پنډ او نري فیلامنټونه د یو بل له څنګ ښویېږي او د لږ تر لږه پوښښ ارام حالت ته ستنېږي. سارکومیرونه او عضلاتي ریشې بیا خپل اعظمي اوږدوالی او غځېدنې وړتیا ترلاسه کوي.

paras.text: Control of Muscle Contraction
paras.urdu: عضلاتی سکڑاؤ کا کنٹرول
paras.pashto: د عضلاتي انقباض کنټرول

paras.text: The contraction of a muscle fibre is normally an all-or-none phenomenon. Once it is stimulated, a muscle fibre will contract to a set length, regardless of intensity of the stimulus above the threshold level.
paras.urdu: عضلاتی ریشے کا سکڑاؤ عموماً سب یا کچھ نہیں کا مظہر ہے۔ تحریک ملنے پر عضلاتی ریشہ مقررہ لمبائی تک سکڑتا ہے، چاہے حدِ آستانہ سے اوپر تحریک کی شدت کچھ بھی ہو۔
paras.pashto: د عضلاتي ریشې انقباض عموماً د ټول یا هېڅ پدیده ده. کله چې تحریک شي، عضلاتي ریشه تر ټاکلي اوږدوالي منقبضېږي، د آستانې له کچې پورته د محرک له شدت پرته.

paras.pashto: شکل 16.19: سارکومیر چې د انقباض حرکت ښیي

paras.text: The question then arises: If fibre contraction is an all-or-none phenomenon, how do we manage the fine control of muscular activity that permits us to lift a pencil on one occasion and a bowling ball on another?
paras.urdu: سوال یہ ہے کہ اگر ریشے کا سکڑاؤ سب یا کچھ نہیں ہے تو ہم عضلات پر باریک کنٹرول سے کبھی پنسل اور کبھی بولنگ کی گیند کیسے اٹھاتے ہیں؟
paras.pashto: پوښتنه دا ده: که د ریشې انقباض ټول یا هېڅ وي، نو د عضلو نازک کنټرول څنګه کوو چې یو وخت پنسل او بل وخت د بولینګ توپ پورته کړو؟

paras.text: Part of the answer has to do with the physical relationship between motor neurons and muscle fibres. The axon of a motor neuron has many branches, each branch terminating at a single muscle fibre. Thus, depending on how many branches it has, one neuron can stimulate several to many different muscle fibres. All the muscle fibres triggered by a single neuron contract simultaneously as a single motor unit. Since a particular muscle may consist of many motor units, the total amount of muscle contraction depends on the number of motor neurons conducting impulses to their motor units in the muscle. If many neurons carry impulses at once, many motor units within the muscle will contract. This causes a stronger over all contraction of the muscle than if only a few motor units are activated.
paras.urdu: جواب کا ایک حصہ حرکی نیورونوں اور عضلاتی ریشوں کے ساختی تعلق میں ہے۔ حرکی نیورون کے ایکسون کی کئی شاخیں ہوتی ہیں، ہر شاخ ایک عضلاتی ریشے پر ختم ہوتی ہے۔ یوں شاخوں کی تعداد کے مطابق ایک نیورون کئی مختلف عضلاتی ریشوں کو تحریک دے سکتا ہے۔ ایک نیورون کے متحرک کردہ تمام ریشے ایک حرکی اکائی کی صورت بیک وقت سکڑتے ہیں۔ ایک عضلہ کئی حرکی اکائیوں پر مشتمل ہو سکتا ہے، اس لیے کل سکڑاؤ ان حرکی نیورونوں کی تعداد پر منحصر ہے جو اکائیوں کو پیغامات دیتے ہیں۔ کئی نیورون بیک وقت پیغامات دیں تو عضلے کی کئی حرکی اکائیاں سکڑتی ہیں۔ اس سے چند اکائیوں کی فعالیت کے مقابلے میں مجموعی سکڑاؤ زیادہ مضبوط ہوتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: د ځواب یوه برخه د حرکي نیورونونو او عضلاتي ریشو له فزیکي اړیکې سره تړاو لري. د حرکي نیورون اکسون ډېرې څانګې لري، چې هره یوه په یوه عضلاتي ریشه پای ته رسېږي. نو د څانګو د شمېر له مخې یو نیورون څو یا ډېرې بېلابېلې عضلاتي ریشې تحریکولای شي. د یوه نیورون له خوا تحریک شوې ټولې ریشې د یوه حرکي واحد په توګه هممهاله منقبضېږي. ځکه چې یوه عضله ډېر حرکي واحدونه لرلای شي، د ټول انقباض اندازه د هغو حرکي نیورونونو په شمېر پورې اړه لري چې خپلو واحدونو ته پیغامونه لېږي. که ډېر نیورونونه یوځای پیغامونه ولېږي، په عضله کې ډېر حرکي واحدونه منقبضېږي. دا د یوازې څو حرکي واحدونو د فعالېدو په پرتله د عضلې پیاوړی ټولیز انقباض جوړوي.

paras.text: Energy of Muscle Contraction
paras.urdu: عضلاتی سکڑاؤ کی توانائی
paras.pashto: د عضلاتي انقباض انرژي

paras.text: Muscle contraction needs energy. The immediate source of energy for the muscle contraction is ATP, stored in the muscle cells. An enzyme ATPase, in the muscle cells breaks ATP to ADP, thus releasing energy for muscle contraction. But much part of the energy comes from carbohydrates or glucose, stored as glycogen in the muscle cells. When muscle contraction begins, glycogen is converted into glucose, which is then broken down to form ATP. The muscle contraction then uses this ATP.
paras.urdu: عضلاتی سکڑاؤ کو توانائی چاہیے۔ عضلاتی سکڑاؤ کی فوری توانائی کا ذریعہ عضلاتی خلیوں میں محفوظ ATP ہے۔ عضلاتی خلیوں میں ATPase خامرہ ATP کو ADP میں توڑ کر سکڑاؤ کے لیے توانائی خارج کرتا ہے۔ لیکن زیادہ توانائی کاربوہائیڈریٹس یا گلوکوز سے آتی ہے، جو عضلاتی خلیوں میں گلائیکوجن کی صورت محفوظ ہیں۔ سکڑاؤ شروع ہونے پر گلائیکوجن گلوکوز میں بدلتا ہے، جو ٹوٹ کر ATP بناتا ہے۔ پھر عضلاتی سکڑاؤ یہ ATP استعمال کرتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: عضلاتي انقباض انرژۍ ته اړتیا لري. د عضلاتي انقباض د انرژۍ سمدستي سرچینه په عضلاتي حجرو کې ساتل شوی ATP دی. په عضلاتي حجرو کې ATPase انزایم ATP په ADP ماتوي او د عضلاتي انقباض لپاره انرژي خوشې کوي. خو د انرژۍ ډېره برخه له کاربوهایډرېټونو یا ګلوکوز څخه راځي، چې په عضلاتي حجرو کې د ګلایکوژن په بڼه ساتل شوي دي. د انقباض په پیل کې ګلایکوژن په ګلوکوز بدلېږي، چې بیا د ATP د جوړولو لپاره ماتېږي. بیا عضلاتي انقباض دا ATP کاروي.

paras.text: We know that in violent exercise, such as running, much energy is needed. Is the normal rate of formation of ATP in muscles fibers adequate for this? Apparently not, but the muscles cells of all vertebrates have a reserve of high-energy phosphate compound, called phosphocreatin. During periods of intensive muscular activity, the phosphocreatin is broken into creatin and a high-energy phosphate group. This group then unites with ADP to form ATP.
paras.urdu: ہم جانتے ہیں کہ دوڑنے جیسی سخت ورزش میں زیادہ توانائی چاہیے۔ کیا عضلاتی ریشوں میں ATP بننے کی معمول کی شرح اس کے لیے کافی ہے؟ بظاہر نہیں، مگر تمام فقاریوں کے عضلاتی خلیوں میں زیادہ توانائی والے فاسفیٹ مرکب فاسفوکریٹین کا ذخیرہ ہوتا ہے۔ شدید عضلاتی سرگرمی میں فاسفوکریٹین، کریٹین اور زیادہ توانائی والے فاسفیٹ گروپ میں ٹوٹتا ہے۔ یہ گروپ پھر ADP سے مل کر ATP بناتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: موږ پوهېږو چې په سخت تمرین لکه منډه کې ډېرې انرژۍ ته اړتیا ده. ایا په عضلاتي ریشو کې د ATP د جوړېدو عادي کچه د دې لپاره بسنه کوي؟ ظاهراً نه، خو د ټولو فقاریه حیواناتو عضلاتي حجرې د فاسفوکریټین په نوم د لوړ انرژي فاسفېټ مرکب زېرمه لري. د سخت عضلاتي فعالیت پر مهال فاسفوکریټین په کریټین او لوړ انرژي فاسفېټ ګروپ ماتېږي. دا ګروپ بیا له ADP سره یوځای کېږي او ATP جوړوي.

paras.text: Of the total energy expended in muscles contraction, only about 35% is utilized for the performance of work; the remaining is liberated in the form of heat, which is employed to maintain body temperature. In cold weather the production of heat can be increased through voluntary muscular activity (walking, rubbing hand together etc) or involuntary by shivering. Conversely, in warm weather, muscular activity is deliberately decreased to reduce heat production.
paras.urdu: عضلاتی سکڑاؤ کی کل توانائی کا صرف تقریباً 35% کام میں استعمال ہوتا ہے؛ باقی حرارت کے طور پر نکل کر جسمانی درجۂ حرارت قائم رکھتا ہے۔ سرد موسم میں اختیاری عضلاتی سرگرمی (چلنے، ہاتھ ملنے وغیرہ) یا غیر اختیاری کپکپی سے حرارت بڑھ سکتی ہے۔ اس کے برعکس گرم موسم میں حرارت کم بنانے کے لیے عضلاتی سرگرمی دانستہ کم کی جاتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: په عضلاتي انقباض کې د مصرف شوې انرژۍ یوازې نږدې 35% د کار لپاره کارېږي؛ پاتې د تودوخې په بڼه خوشې کېږي او د بدن تودوخه ساتي. په سړه هوا کې د ارادي عضلاتي فعالیت (ګرځېدو، د لاسونو موښلو او نورو) یا غیر ارادي لړزې له لارې تودوخه زیاتېدای شي. برعکس، په ګرمه هوا کې د تودوخې د تولید د کمولو لپاره عضلاتي فعالیت په قصدي ډول کمېږي.

sections.heading: 16.3.5 Muscle problems
sections.title: 16.3.5 Muscle problems
sections.text:
I. Cramps:

Muscle cramps are sudden, involuntary contractions or spasms in one or more muscles. They often occur after exercise or at night, lasting a few seconds to several minutes. Writer's cramp is a familiar example of temporary contractures. Muscle cramps can be caused by nerves that malfunction. Other causes are, straining or overusing a muscle, dehydration, lack of minerals in diet or the depletion of minerals in body, and not enough blood getting to muscles.

Fig: 16.20 Cramps are involuntary contractions or spasms in one or more muscles.

ii. Muscle fatigue:

Muscle fatigue is a condition of the muscle in which its capacity to produce maximum contraction is reduced even though the muscle still may be receiving stimuli. Availability of ATP declines during contraction and a total lack of ATP results in contractures, states of continuous contraction because the cross bridges are unable to detach. Although excessive intracellular accumulation of lactic acid (which causes the muscles to ache and raises H⁺) alters contractile proteins, other ionic imbalances also contribute to muscle fatigue. In general, intense exercise of short duration produces fatigue rapidly via ionic disturbances, but recovery is also rapid. In contrast to short-duration exercise, the slow-developing fatigue of prolonged low-intensity exercise may require several hours for complete recovery.

iii. Tetany:

Tetany is a symptom characterized by muscle cramps, spasms or tremors. These repetitive actions of the muscles happen when muscle contracts uncontrollably. Tetany may occur in any muscle of the body, such as those in face, fingers or calves. The muscle cramping associated with tetany can be long lasting and painful. A common cause of tetany is very low levels of calcium in the body.

Tetanus:

Tetanus is infection of the nervous system with the potentially deadly bacteria Clostridium tetani. Spores of the bacteria C. tetani live in the soil and are found around the world. In the spore form, C. tetani may remain inactive in the soil, but it can remain infectious for more than 40 years. Infection begins when the spores enter the body through an injury or wound. The spores release bacteria that spread and make a poison called tetanospasmin. This poison blocks nerve signals from the spinal cord to the muscles, causing severe muscle spasms. The spasms can be so powerful that they tear the muscles or cause fractures of the spine.

Fig: 16.21 Clostridium tetani

sections.heading: KEY POINTS — Support and Movement
sections.title: KEY POINTS — Support and Movement
sections.text:
The skeleton in animals contributes in upholding and sustaining the body against gravity and other external forces.
The vertebrate skeleton is composed either of cartilage or bone.
Cartilage consists of cells called chondrocytes and a tough, flexible matrix made of type II collagen and it is without blood vessels.
Bone is a living hard and strong structure consisting of a hard ground substance or matrix and cells.
Bones are composed of osteoblasts (cells that help form bone), and osteoclasts (cells that help eat away old bone) and osteocytes which are mature osteoblasts.
Human skeleton consists of 206 individual bones which are grouped into two general divisions; axial skeleton, the basic framework of the body and appendicular skeleton, the extremities.
The human skull is composed of 22 bones, besides 6 tiny ear bones and one hyoid bone.
In human, there are 33 vertebrae. Seven cervical vertebrae, 12 thoracic vertebrae; 5 lumber vertebrae; 5 sacral vertebrae and at the end of the vertebral column is the coccyx or tail bone which consists of 4 small fused vertebrae.
In human there are twelve pairs of ribs, one pair articulating with each of the thoracic vertebrae forming a cage that encloses the heart and lungs.
The appendicular skeleton consists of pectoral girdles with forelimbs and pelvic girdle with hind limbs.
The sites where two or more bones meet are called joints or articulations.
Deformities of skeleton may be genetic, hormonal or due to the effects of nutrient deficiency.
A fracture means broken bone.
Simple fractures are those in which the skin is intact.
Compound fracture is an open fracture: if the bone ends penetrate the skin and form a wound.
A dislocated joint is a joint that slips out of place.
Based on location, three types of muscles are skeletal, cardiac, and smooth.
The skeletal muscle consists of muscles bundle, which are further composed of huge elongated cells called muscles fibre..
The immediate source of energy for the muscle contraction is ATP, stored in the muscle cells. An enzyme ATPase, in the muscle cells breaks ATP to ADP, thus releasing energy for muscle contraction.
Muscle fatigue is a condition of the muscle in which its capacity to produce maximum contraction is reduced even though the muscle still may be receiving stimuli.
Muscle cramps are sudden, involuntary contractions or spasms in one or more muscles.
Tetany is a symptom characterized by muscle cramps, spasms or tremors.
Tetanus is a infection of the nervous system caused by a deadly bacteria Clostridium tetani.

paras.text: The skeleton in animals contributes in upholding and sustaining the body against gravity and other external forces.
paras.urdu: حیوانوں کا ڈھانچا کششِ ثقل اور بیرونی قوتوں کے مقابل جسم کو سہارا دیتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: د حیواناتو اسکلېټ د جاذبې او نورو بهرنیو ځواکونو پر وړاندې د بدن په ساتلو کې مرسته کوي.

paras.text: The vertebrate skeleton is composed either of cartilage or bone.
paras.urdu: فقاریوں کا ڈھانچا غضروف یا ہڈی سے بنتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: د فقاریه اسکلېټ له غضروف یا هډوکي جوړ دی.

paras.text: Cartilage consists of cells called chondrocytes and a tough, flexible matrix made of type II collagen and it is without blood vessels.
paras.urdu: غضروف کونڈروسائٹس اور ٹائپ II کولیجن کے مضبوط لچک دار میٹرکس سے بنتا ہے؛ اس میں خون کی نالیاں نہیں۔
paras.pashto: غضروف کونډروسایټونه او د دوهم ډول کولاژن کلک انعطاف منونکی ماتریکس لري او د وینې رګونه نه لري.

paras.text: Bone is a living hard and strong structure consisting of a hard ground substance or matrix and cells.
paras.urdu: ہڈی زندہ سخت اور مضبوط ساخت ہے، جو سخت بنیادی مادے یا میٹرکس اور خلیوں سے بنتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: هډوکی ژوندی کلک او پیاوړی جوړښت دی چې له کلکې بنسټیزې مادې یا ماتریکس او حجرو جوړ دی.

paras.text: Bones are composed of osteoblasts (cells that help form bone), and osteoclasts (cells that help eat away old bone) and osteocytes which are mature osteoblasts.
paras.urdu: ہڈیوں میں ہڈی بنانے والے اوسٹیوبلاسٹس، پرانی ہڈی تحلیل کرنے والے اوسٹیوکلاسٹس اور پختہ اوسٹیوبلاسٹس یعنی اوسٹیوسائٹس ہوتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: هډوکي اوستیوبلاسټونه (هډوکی جوړوي)، اوستیوکلاسټونه (زوړ هډوکی ماتوي) او اوستیوسایټونه، چې پاخه اوستیوبلاسټونه دي، لري.

paras.text: Human skeleton consists of 206 individual bones which are grouped into two general divisions; axial skeleton, the basic framework of the body and appendicular skeleton, the extremities.
paras.urdu: انسانی ڈھانچے کی 206 ہڈیاں دو حصوں میں ہیں: محوری ڈھانچا، جسم کا بنیادی فریم، اور ضمیمی ڈھانچا، اطراف کے اعضا۔
paras.pashto: د انسان د اسکلېټ 206 هډوکي په دوو برخو وېشل کېږي: محوري اسکلېټ، د بدن بنسټیز چوکاټ، او ضمیموي اسکلېټ، اندامونه.

paras.text: The human skull is composed of 22 bones, besides 6 tiny ear bones and one hyoid bone.
paras.urdu: انسانی کھوپڑی میں 22 ہڈیاں، اس کے علاوہ کان کی 6 چھوٹی ہڈیاں اور ایک ہائیوئڈ ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د انسان کوپړۍ 22 هډوکي لري، سربېره پر دې د غوږ 6 واړه هډوکي او یو هایویډ هډوکی شته.

paras.text: In human, there are 33 vertebrae. Seven cervical vertebrae, 12 thoracic vertebrae; 5 lumber vertebrae; 5 sacral vertebrae and at the end of the vertebral column is the coccyx or tail bone which consists of 4 small fused vertebrae.
paras.urdu: انسان میں 33 مہرے ہیں: 7 عنقی، 12 صدری، 5 قطنی، 5 سیکرل اور آخر میں 4 چھوٹے جڑے مہروں کا کوکسکس یا دم کی ہڈی۔
paras.pashto: په انسان کې 33 مهرې دي: 7 عنقي، 12 صدري، 5 قطني، 5 سکرل او په پای کې کوکسیکس یا د لکۍ هډوکی چې له 4 وړو یوځای شوو مهرو جوړ دی.

paras.text: In human there are twelve pairs of ribs, one pair articulating with each of the thoracic vertebrae forming a cage that encloses the heart and lungs.
paras.urdu: انسان میں پسلیوں کے بارہ جوڑے ہیں، ہر صدری مہرے سے ایک جوڑا جڑ کر دل اور پھیپھڑوں کا پنجرہ بناتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: په انسان کې د پښتيو دولس جوړې دي، چې له هرې صدري مهرې سره یوه جوړه نښلي او د زړه او سږو شاوخوا قفس جوړوي.

paras.text: The appendicular skeleton consists of pectoral girdles with forelimbs and pelvic girdle with hind limbs.
paras.urdu: ضمیمی ڈھانچا اگلے اعضا کے ساتھ کندھوں کی پٹیوں اور پچھلے اعضا کے ساتھ شرونی پٹی سے بنتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: ضمیموي اسکلېټ د مخکنیو اندامونو سره صدري کمربندونه او د شاتنیو اندامونو سره حوضي کمربند لري.

paras.text: The sites where two or more bones meet are called joints or articulations.
paras.urdu: دو یا زیادہ ہڈیوں کے ملنے کی جگہیں جوڑ ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د دوو یا زیاتو هډوکو د یوځای کېدو ځایونه بندونه دي.

paras.text: Deformities of skeleton may be genetic, hormonal or due to the effects of nutrient deficiency.
paras.urdu: ڈھانچے کے بگاڑ موروثی، ہارمونی یا غذائی کمی سے ہو سکتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د اسکلېټ بدشکلۍ جنتیکي، هورموني یا د غذايي موادو د کمښت له امله کېدای شي.

paras.text: A fracture means broken bone.
paras.urdu: فریکچر کا مطلب ٹوٹی ہڈی ہے۔
paras.pashto: فریکچر د مات هډوکي معنا لري.

paras.text: Simple fractures are those in which the skin is intact.
paras.urdu: سادہ فریکچر میں جلد سلامت رہتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: په ساده ماتېدنه کې پوستکی روغ وي.

paras.text: Compound fracture is an open fracture: if the bone ends penetrate the skin and form a wound.
paras.urdu: مرکب فریکچر کھلا فریکچر ہے، جب ہڈی کے سرے جلد پھاڑ کر زخم بنائیں۔
paras.pashto: مرکبه ماتېدنه پرانیستې ماتېدنه ده، چې د هډوکي سرونه پوستکی سوری کړي او زخم جوړ کړي.

paras.text: A dislocated joint is a joint that slips out of place.
paras.urdu: اترا جوڑ اپنی جگہ سے نکل جاتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: بې ځایه شوی بند له خپل ځایه وځي.

paras.text: Based on location, three types of muscles are skeletal, cardiac, and smooth.
paras.urdu: مقام کے لحاظ سے عضلات کی تین اقسام ڈھانچائی، قلبی اور ہموار ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د موقعیت له مخې عضلې درې ډوله دي: اسکلېټي، قلبي او نرمې.

paras.text: The skeletal muscle consists of muscles bundle, which are further composed of huge elongated cells called muscles fibre..
paras.urdu: ڈھانچائی عضلہ گچھوں سے بنتا ہے، جو عضلاتی ریشے نامی بڑے لمبے خلیوں پر مشتمل ہیں۔
paras.pashto: اسکلېټي عضله له ګېډیو جوړه ده چې د عضلاتي ریشو په نوم لویې اوږدې حجرې لري.

paras.text: The immediate source of energy for the muscle contraction is ATP, stored in the muscle cells. An enzyme ATPase, in the muscle cells breaks ATP to ADP, thus releasing energy for muscle contraction.
paras.urdu: عضلاتی سکڑاؤ کی فوری توانائی خلیوں میں محفوظ ATP ہے۔ ATPase اسے ADP میں توڑ کر توانائی خارج کرتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: د عضلاتي انقباض د انرژۍ سمدستي سرچینه په حجرو کې ساتل شوی ATP دی. ATPase یې په ADP ماتوي او د انقباض انرژي خوشې کوي.

paras.text: Muscle fatigue is a condition of the muscle in which its capacity to produce maximum contraction is reduced even though the muscle still may be receiving stimuli.
paras.urdu: عضلاتی تھکن میں تحریک ملنے کے باوجود زیادہ سے زیادہ سکڑاؤ کی صلاحیت کم ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: په عضلاتي ستړیا کې د تحریکونو له رسېدو سره سره د اعظمي انقباض وړتیا کمېږي.

paras.text: Muscle cramps are sudden, involuntary contractions or spasms in one or more muscles.
paras.urdu: عضلاتی اینٹھن ایک یا زیادہ عضلات کا اچانک غیر اختیاری سکڑاؤ یا تشنج ہے۔
paras.pashto: عضلاتي کرامپونه په یوه یا زیاتو عضلو کې ناڅاپي غیر ارادي انقباضونه یا تشنجونه دي.

paras.text: Tetany is a symptom characterized by muscle cramps, spasms or tremors.
paras.urdu: ٹیٹنی کی علامت عضلاتی اینٹھن، تشنج یا لرزش ہے۔
paras.pashto: ټیټني هغه نښه ده چې عضلاتي کرامپونه، تشنجونه یا رپېدل پکې وي.

paras.text: Tetanus is a infection of the nervous system caused by a deadly bacteria Clostridium tetani.
paras.urdu: تشنج مہلک بیکٹیریا کلوسٹریڈیم ٹیٹانی سے اعصابی نظام کا انفیکشن ہے۔
paras.pashto: تیتانوس د وژونکې بکتریا کلوسټریډیم ټیټاني له امله د عصبي سیسټم انتان دی.

mcqs.q: The disorder in which bones are porous and thin but bone composition is normal is;
mcqs.explanation: Osteoporosis involves loss of bone mass and deterioration of its structure, making bones thinner and more fragile.

mcqs.q: The organic portion of bone’s matrix is important in providing all but;
mcqs.explanation: Organic collagen contributes flexibility and tensile resistance; mineral salts provide the characteristic hardness.

mcqs.q: The remodeling of bone is a function of which cells?
mcqs.explanation: Osteoclasts resorb old bone and osteoblasts form new bone during remodeling.

mcqs.q: In skeletal muscle, calcium facilitates contraction by binding to
mcqs.explanation: Calcium binds troponin, allowing tropomyosin to shift and expose actin’s myosin-binding sites.

mcqs.q: Which of the following statements concerning the role of Ca⁺² in the contraction of skeletal muscle is correct?
opts: The mitochondria act as a store of Ca⁺⁺ for the contractile process
Ca⁺² entry across the plasma membrane is important in sustaining the contraction of skeletal muscle
A rise in intracellular Ca⁺² allows actin to interact with myosin
The tension of a skeletal muscle fibre is partly regulated by G proteins muscle
mcqs.explanation: Increased calcium in the muscle-fibre cytoplasm permits the actin–myosin interaction through the regulatory proteins.

mcqs.q: The function of the T tubules in muscle contraction is to
opts: release Ca⁺² into the cell interior and then pick it up again
make the action potential deep into the muscle cells
to hamper the the nerve impulse
mcqs.explanation: T tubules conduct the action potential into the fibre; the sarcoplasmic reticulum stores, releases and takes up calcium.

mcqs.q: The sites where the motor nerve impulse is transmitted from the nerve endings to the skeletal muscle cell membranes are the:
mcqs.explanation: A neuromuscular junction is the communication site between a motor neuron and a skeletal muscle fibre.

mcqs.q: Myoglobin has a special function in muscle tissue.
opts: it holds a reserve supply of oxygen in the muscle
mcqs.explanation: Myoglobin binds oxygen and provides a reserve in muscle cells.

shortQuestions.q: Name the cranial and facial bones.
steps: Cranial bones: frontal, occipital, sphenoid and ethmoid are unpaired; parietal and temporal are paired. This gives eight cranial bones.
Facial bones: mandible and vomer are unpaired; maxilla, zygomatic, lacrimal, nasal, inferior nasal concha and palatine are paired. This gives fourteen facial bones.
shortQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Cranial bones: frontal, occipital, sphenoid and ethmoid are unpaired; parietal and temporal are paired. This gives eight cranial bones.
  2. Facial bones: mandible and vomer are unpaired; maxilla, zygomatic, lacrimal, nasal, inferior nasal concha and palatine are paired. This gives fourteen facial bones.
Answer: Eight cranial bones form the cranium and fourteen facial bones form the face, as listed in Table16.3.
shortQuestions.plainAnswer: Eight cranial bones form the cranium and fourteen facial bones form the face, as listed in Table16.3.

shortQuestions.q: What is the function of the intervertebral discs?
steps: The discs lie between adjacent vertebral bodies.
Their resilient structure absorbs shocks and distributes loads.
They also allow limited movement while helping connect and support the vertebral column.
shortQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. The discs lie between adjacent vertebral bodies.
  2. Their resilient structure absorbs shocks and distributes loads.
  3. They also allow limited movement while helping connect and support the vertebral column.
Answer: Intervertebral discs cushion the vertebrae, absorb shocks and permit controlled flexibility.
shortQuestions.plainAnswer: Intervertebral discs cushion the vertebrae, absorb shocks and permit controlled flexibility.

shortQuestions.q: Briefly describe the impairment of function seen in cleft palate.
steps: A cleft palate leaves an opening in the roof of the mouth.
This can make feeding difficult and interfere with normal speech.
Associated middle-ear problems may affect hearing.
shortQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. A cleft palate leaves an opening in the roof of the mouth.
  2. This can make feeding difficult and interfere with normal speech.
  3. Associated middle-ear problems may affect hearing.
Answer: Cleft palate can impair feeding, speech and hearing; effects vary between individuals.

Source: Great Ormond Street Hospital — cleft lip and palate.
shortQuestions.plainAnswer: Cleft palate can impair feeding, speech and hearing; effects vary between individuals.

steps: Bone is living connective tissue containing cells embedded in a hard, mineralized matrix.
Its organic component is chiefly collagen, which contributes flexibility and tensile strength. Inorganic calcium-phosphate-rich mineral gives hardness.
Osteoblasts produce bone matrix; osteocytes are mature bone cells within it; osteoclasts resorb bone during remodeling.
Bone has blood vessels that support its living cells and metabolic exchange.

The chapter gives two approximate organic/inorganic ratios in different paragraphs; use the qualitative distinction between collagen and mineral rather than treating the two printed ratios as identical.

SpaceBook learning answer

  2. Its organic component is chiefly collagen, which contributes flexibility and tensile strength. Inorganic calcium-phosphate-rich mineral gives hardness.
  3. Osteoblasts produce bone matrix; osteocytes are mature bone cells within it; osteoclasts resorb bone during remodeling.
  4. Bone has blood vessels that support its living cells and metabolic exchange.
  5. The chapter gives two approximate organic/inorganic ratios in different paragraphs; use the qualitative distinction between collagen and mineral rather than treating the two printed ratios as identical.
Answer: Bone consists of living cells in a collagen-and-mineral matrix and is continually maintained and remodeled.

Reference: OpenStax — bone structure.

longQuestions.q: Describe major divisions of human axial skeleton
steps: The skull protects the brain and includes the cranial and facial bones, with associated ear ossicles and hyoid discussed in the chapter.
The vertebral column supports the trunk and protects the spinal cord. Its regions are cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral and coccygeal.
The thoracic cage consists of ribs and sternum and protects the heart and lungs.
There are twelve rib pairs: seven attach directly to the sternum, three indirectly, and the final two have no anterior attachment.

SpaceBook learning answer

  3. The thoracic cage consists of ribs and sternum and protects the heart and lungs.
  4. There are twelve rib pairs: seven attach directly to the sternum, three indirectly, and the final two have no anterior attachment.
Answer: The axial skeleton comprises the skull, vertebral column and thoracic cage.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: The axial skeleton comprises the skull, vertebral column and thoracic cage.

longQuestions.q: What are types of fractures? Describe the repair process of a simple fracture.
steps: A simple or closed fracture leaves the skin intact; an open or compound fracture communicates with a skin wound.
Hematoma formation: torn vessels bleed and a clot forms at the break.
Fibrocartilaginous callus formation: new vessels and repair cells enter; a soft callus bridges the broken ends.
Bony callus formation: the soft callus is replaced by a harder bridge of spongy bone.
Remodeling: bone is reorganized in response to mechanical stresses, restoring its structure.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. A simple or closed fracture leaves the skin intact; an open or compound fracture communicates with a skin wound.
  2. Hematoma formation: torn vessels bleed and a clot forms at the break.
  3. Fibrocartilaginous callus formation: new vessels and repair cells enter; a soft callus bridges the broken ends.
  4. Bony callus formation: the soft callus is replaced by a harder bridge of spongy bone.
  5. Remodeling: bone is reorganized in response to mechanical stresses, restoring its structure.
Answer: The two source fracture types are closed and open; repair proceeds through hematoma, soft callus, bony callus and remodeling.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: The two source fracture types are closed and open; repair proceeds through hematoma, soft callus, bony callus and remodeling.

longQuestions.q: Compare smooth, cardiac, and skeletal muscles.
steps: Skeletal muscle attaches to the skeleton, has long unbranched striated fibres with many nuclei, and is normally under voluntary control. It moves the body and maintains posture.
Cardiac muscle occurs in the heart, is striated and branched, and contracts involuntarily and rhythmically to pump blood. The source describes a single nucleus.
Smooth muscle occurs in walls of hollow organs and vessels. Its spindle-shaped cells have a central nucleus, lack striations and are involuntary.

SpaceBook learning answer
