  2. Cardiac muscle occurs in the heart, is striated and branched, and contracts involuntarily and rhythmically to pump blood. The source describes a single nucleus.
  3. Smooth muscle occurs in walls of hollow organs and vessels. Its spindle-shaped cells have a central nucleus, lack striations and are involuntary.
Answer: Skeletal: voluntary body movement; cardiac: involuntary heart pumping; smooth: involuntary action in hollow organs and vessels.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: Skeletal: voluntary body movement; cardiac: involuntary heart pumping; smooth: involuntary action in hollow organs and vessels.

longQuestions.q: Explain the ultra-structure of human skeletal muscles.
steps: A skeletal muscle contains bundles of long muscle fibres. Each fibre has a sarcolemma surrounding sarcoplasm with peripheral nuclei, mitochondria, glycogen and myoglobin.
T tubules carry excitation inward, while the sarcoplasmic reticulum stores and releases calcium.
The fibre contains myofibrils composed of repeating sarcomeres between successive Z lines.
Thin actin filaments and thick myosin filaments form the banding pattern; thin filaments also contain troponin and tropomyosin.
The A band corresponds to the thick-filament length, the I band contains thin filaments without thick overlap, and the H zone is the central thick-only region. The M line lies centrally.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. A skeletal muscle contains bundles of long muscle fibres. Each fibre has a sarcolemma surrounding sarcoplasm with peripheral nuclei, mitochondria, glycogen and myoglobin.
  2. T tubules carry excitation inward, while the sarcoplasmic reticulum stores and releases calcium.
  3. The fibre contains myofibrils composed of repeating sarcomeres between successive Z lines.
  4. Thin actin filaments and thick myosin filaments form the banding pattern; thin filaments also contain troponin and tropomyosin.
  5. The A band corresponds to the thick-filament length, the I band contains thin filaments without thick overlap, and the H zone is the central thick-only region. The M line lies centrally.
Answer: Skeletal muscle is organized as muscle → bundles → fibres → myofibrils → sarcomeres → thick and thin filaments.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: Skeletal muscle is organized as muscle → bundles → fibres → myofibrils → sarcomeres → thick and thin filaments.

longQuestions.q: Explain the sliding filament theory of contraction using appropriately labeled diagrams of a relaxed and a contracted sarcomere.
steps: Calcium exposes binding sites through the thin-filament regulatory proteins.
Myosin cross-bridges bind actin and pull thin filaments toward the centre. ATP supports repeated attachment, movement and detachment.
The Z lines move closer together; the sarcomere, I bands and H zone shorten. The A band and individual filament lengths remain essentially unchanged.
When excitation stops and calcium returns to the sarcoplasmic reticulum, active cross-bridge cycling stops and the fibre can relax.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Calcium exposes binding sites through the thin-filament regulatory proteins.
  2. Myosin cross-bridges bind actin and pull thin filaments toward the centre. ATP supports repeated attachment, movement and detachment.
  3. The Z lines move closer together; the sarcomere, I bands and H zone shorten. The A band and individual filament lengths remain essentially unchanged.
  4. When excitation stops and calcium returns to the sarcoplasmic reticulum, active cross-bridge cycling stops and the fibre can relax.
Answer: Contraction results from greater overlap of actin and myosin, not shortening of the filaments themselves.

Mechanism reference: OpenStax — muscle contraction and relaxation.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: Contraction results from greater overlap of actin and myosin, not shortening of the filaments themselves.

longQuestions.q: Describe the structure of a sarcomere and indicate the relationship of the sarcomere to the myofilament
steps: A sarcomere extends from one Z line to the next and is a repeating contractile unit in a myofibril.
Thin actin filaments attach to the Z lines and extend toward the centre; thick myosin filaments occupy the central region.
Their arrangement creates I bands, an A band, an H zone and an M line.
Myofilaments are the protein filaments within each sarcomere; many sarcomeres arranged end to end form a myofibril.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. A sarcomere extends from one Z line to the next and is a repeating contractile unit in a myofibril.
  2. Thin actin filaments attach to the Z lines and extend toward the centre; thick myosin filaments occupy the central region.
  3. Their arrangement creates I bands, an A band, an H zone and an M line.
  4. Myofilaments are the protein filaments within each sarcomere; many sarcomeres arranged end to end form a myofibril.
Answer: A sarcomere is a structural unit built from overlapping thick and thin myofilaments, bounded by two Z lines.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: A sarcomere is a structural unit built from overlapping thick and thin myofilaments, bounded by two Z lines.

activities.title: Identify the bones of the pelvic girdle, pectoral girdle, arms and leg by using the model of human skeleton.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: On the model, identify the paired hip bones (ilium, ischium and pubis), scapulae and clavicles, humerus, radius, ulna, femur, tibia and fibula. Then locate wrist, palm and finger bones and ankle, foot and toe bones. Use the model’s labels to distinguish the girdles from the free limbs.

activities.title: Compare the structure of skeleton, smooth and cardiac muscles with the help of prepared slides.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Record the actual slides: skeletal muscle has long parallel striated fibres and multiple peripheral nuclei; cardiac muscle has branching striated cells and intercalated discs; smooth muscle has spindle-shaped cells, a central nucleus and no striations. Do not invent features that are not visible at the available magnification.

activities.title: Draw a diagram of sarcomere and label its parts.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Draw two Z lines, thin actin filaments attached to each, and central thick myosin filaments. Label the sarcomere, A band, I bands, H zone, M line and the overlap region. The relaxed/contracted schematic in long answer vi provides a starting layout.

activities.title: Justify how the main functions of the skeleton are to act as a system of rods and levers, which are moved by the muscles.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Bones act as rigid levers, joints provide pivot points and contracting muscles apply pulling forces through their attachments. The resulting lever movement changes the position of body parts. The skeleton also supports and protects the body.

activities.title: Justify why do the muscles pull but do not push.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Muscle contraction develops tension that pulls on attachments. Active shortening does not push those attachments apart. Opposing muscles or external forces produce the reverse movement.

activities.title: Relate the bipedal posture of man with his skeleton and musculature.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: The vertebral column and pelvis support an upright trunk, the lower limbs bear weight, and the feet provide a base of support. Coordinated trunk, hip and leg muscles maintain balance and produce walking movements.

activities.title: Name the techniques for joint transplantation.
activities.desc:
SpaceBook learning answer: The intended term is joint replacement or arthroplasty: partial replacement replaces part of a damaged joint, while total replacement replaces the relevant joint surfaces with artificial components. These are prosthetic replacements, rather than routine transplantation of an entire donor joint.

Source: NIAMS — osteoarthritis surgery.

activities.title: Justify the use of calcium in teenage and twenties can be a preventive action against osteoporosis.
activities.desc:
SpaceBook learning answer: Adequate calcium and vitamin D support development of peak bone mass during growth and early adulthood. Building stronger bones provides a better reserve against later bone loss. Nutrition is one factor alongside physical activity and other influences; the question does not imply that everyone needs supplements.

Source: NIAMS — osteoporosis and bone health.

activities.title: Reason out the rigor mortis.
activities.desc:
SpaceBook learning answer: After death, ATP production stops. Without fresh ATP, myosin cannot detach normally from actin, so cross-bridges remain attached and the muscles become stiff.

Source: OpenStax — muscle contraction and relaxation.

activities.title: Relate improper posture to bone/joint problems.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Posture changes how body weight and muscle forces are distributed. Sustained awkward positioning can increase strain on particular muscles, ligaments and joints. Balanced alignment and changing position help distribute loads; posture alone does not explain every skeletal disorder.

steps: A sarcomere extends from one Z line to the next and is a repeating contractile unit in a myofibril.
Thin actin filaments attach to the Z lines and extend toward the centre; thick myosin filaments occupy the central region.
Their arrangement creates I bands, an A band, an H zone and an M line.
Myofilaments are the protein filaments within each sarcomere; many sarcomeres arranged end to end form a myofibril.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. A sarcomere extends from one Z line to the next and is a repeating contractile unit in a myofibril.
  2. Thin actin filaments attach to the Z lines and extend toward the centre; thick myosin filaments occupy the central region.
  3. Their arrangement creates I bands, an A band, an H zone and an M line.
  4. Myofilaments are the protein filaments within each sarcomere; many sarcomeres arranged end to end form a myofibril.
Answer: A sarcomere is a structural unit built from overlapping thick and thin myofilaments, bounded by two Z lines.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: A sarcomere is a structural unit built from overlapping thick and thin myofilaments, bounded by two Z lines.

activities.title: Identify the bones of the pelvic girdle, pectoral girdle, arms and leg by using the model of human skeleton.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: On the model, identify the paired hip bones (ilium, ischium and pubis), scapulae and clavicles, humerus, radius, ulna, femur, tibia and fibula. Then locate wrist, palm and finger bones and ankle, foot and toe bones. Use the model’s labels to distinguish the girdles from the free limbs.

activities.title: Compare the structure of skeleton, smooth and cardiac muscles with the help of prepared slides.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Record the actual slides: skeletal muscle has long parallel striated fibres and multiple peripheral nuclei; cardiac muscle has branching striated cells and intercalated discs; smooth muscle has spindle-shaped cells, a central nucleus and no striations. Do not invent features that are not visible at the available magnification.

activities.title: Draw a diagram of sarcomere and label its parts.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Draw two Z lines, thin actin filaments attached to each, and central thick myosin filaments. Label the sarcomere, A band, I bands, H zone, M line and the overlap region. The relaxed/contracted schematic in long answer vi provides a starting layout.

activities.title: Justify how the main functions of the skeleton are to act as a system of rods and levers, which are moved by the muscles.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Bones act as rigid levers, joints provide pivot points and contracting muscles apply pulling forces through their attachments. The resulting lever movement changes the position of body parts. The skeleton also supports and protects the body.

activities.title: Justify why do the muscles pull but do not push.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Muscle contraction develops tension that pulls on attachments. Active shortening does not push those attachments apart. Opposing muscles or external forces produce the reverse movement.

activities.title: Relate the bipedal posture of man with his skeleton and musculature.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: The vertebral column and pelvis support an upright trunk, the lower limbs bear weight, and the feet provide a base of support. Coordinated trunk, hip and leg muscles maintain balance and produce walking movements.

activities.title: Name the techniques for joint transplantation.
activities.desc:
SpaceBook learning answer: The intended term is joint replacement or arthroplasty: partial replacement replaces part of a damaged joint, while total replacement replaces the relevant joint surfaces with artificial components. These are prosthetic replacements, rather than routine transplantation of an entire donor joint.

Source: NIAMS — osteoarthritis surgery.

activities.title: Justify the use of calcium in teenage and twenties can be a preventive action against osteoporosis.
activities.desc:
SpaceBook learning answer: Adequate calcium and vitamin D support development of peak bone mass during growth and early adulthood. Building stronger bones provides a better reserve against later bone loss. Nutrition is one factor alongside physical activity and other influences; the question does not imply that everyone needs supplements.

Source: NIAMS — osteoporosis and bone health.

activities.title: Reason out the rigor mortis.
activities.desc:
SpaceBook learning answer: After death, ATP production stops. Without fresh ATP, myosin cannot detach normally from actin, so cross-bridges remain attached and the muscles become stiff.

Source: OpenStax — muscle contraction and relaxation.

activities.title: Relate improper posture to bone/joint problems.
activities.desc: SpaceBook learning answer: Posture changes how body weight and muscle forces are distributed. Sustained awkward positioning can increase strain on particular muscles, ligaments and joints. Balanced alignment and changing position help distribute loads; posture alone does not explain every skeletal disorder.
